headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared file-based workflows and broad egress, while capability conflict is limited by non-overlapping write surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon can ingest documents, PDFs, HTML, MHTML, XLSX, DOC/DOCX and uses a web UI plus ./ktem_app_data, so attacker-controlled content could be fed into opik if outputs are copied or shared. opik exposes a REST API and broad egress, but no direct bridge is documented, so the interaction is inferred and uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF kotaemon outputs are pasted into opik prompts or evaluation inputs, injection content can propagate.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or clipboard, attacker-controlled file text can bridge them.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted documents in kotaemon.
Use a separate staging folder for files before opik evaluation.
Strip instructions from retrieved text before passing it onward.
Add a manual review step for any content copied between tools.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and many document types, while opik has broad network egress and a REST API. If they share a workspace or operator workflow, sensitive document contents or secrets touched by kotaemon could be forwarded into opik outputs or telemetry. No direct shared filesystem is documented, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF kotaemon processes documents containing secrets or chat transcripts and those artifacts are sent to opik, leakage occurs.
IF opik transmits evaluation payloads to a third-party backend, copied sensitive content can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Do not route API keys or transcripts into opik inputs.
Redact secrets from kotaemon outputs before export.
Use separate per-tool workspaces with no shared files.
Review outbound requests from opik for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction in the integration layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon can write to ./ktem_app_data and supports multiple instances, but opik only shows a REST API and no filesystem write surface. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is operator-mediated data flow, not concurrent mutation of the same resource.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same writable directory, file conflicts become possible.
IF opik is extended with filesystem writes, the conflict surface increases.
mitigations: Keep separate directories for each agent.
Avoid mounting kotaemon data into opik containers.
Run only one writer per workspace.
Check for accidental shared volumes before launch.
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared mutable store is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces retrieved documents, citations, and chat transcripts that opik could consume for evaluation or observability. If opik treats those outputs as authoritative without verification, retrieval mistakes or hallucinated citations can cascade into incorrect reports or actions. The pair lacks documented guardrails, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF opik ingests kotaemon-generated answers without a verification step, errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation trusts evaluated outputs as facts, incorrect actions may follow.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on kotaemon outputs.
Compare retrieved citations against source documents.
Mark opik inputs as untrusted by default.
Log provenance for every transferred answer.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys, chat transcripts, and many document types, while opik is an observability/evaluation tool with broad egress. If regulated or sensitive content from kotaemon is sent into opik, retention and residency obligations may diverge. No specific certifications or residency guarantees are documented for either agent, so the mismatch risk is present but not proven high.
conditions: IF kotaemon processes regulated documents and opik stores them under a different retention policy, compliance drift occurs.
IF EU personal data is exported through opik to a non-EU backend, residency obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to opik.
Exclude secrets and regulated records from evaluation runs.
Set explicit retention limits for both tools.
Document where each tool stores logs and traces.
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion workflows across both systems.
